title: Police In New York Warn Of More Killings Following Death Of Kirk - NewsBreak
text:
By Bobby Welber ,
6 hours ago
Following the murder of Charlie Kirk, police in New York State are warning about more violence and killings.
Charlie Kirk, who has a small tie to the Hudson Valley, was fatally shot last Wednesday.
New York State Officials Fear Civil War
Getty Images The far-right activist was killed during an outdoor rally at Utah Valley University. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul held a bipartisan emergency meeting in response.
Top elected officials are worried about more violence. According to Hochul’s office, after Kirk’s murder, online calls for “Civil War” skyrocketed. Mentions about a Civil War increased from under 50,000 to more than 200,000 in just two days.
“I convened a bipartisan group of leaders to discuss what is truly necessary in this moment: reducing the temperature of inflammatory rhetoric that leads to violence and ensuring our communities are safe and tolerant places for all,” Hochul said.
Hochul hopes there’s a cooling of political violence. Saying that Democrats and Republicans can debate their differences without demeaning each other.
For all the news that the Hudson Valley is sharing, make sure to follow Hudson Valley Post on Facebook, and download the Hudson Valley Post Mobile App
NYPD Warns Of More Violence, Killings Getty Images Unfortunately, that might not be the case. The NYPD is warning of more violence against business leaders, politicians, and other top officials following the killings of Kirk and UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
ABC obtained an internal memo from the NYPD that warns of future attacks:
The targeted attack occurred against the backdrop of an increasingly volatile threat environment in the U.S. amid ongoing concerns over the targeting of and violent threats persistently aimed at prominent political figures, CEOs, public officials, and other dignitaries. These individuals likely remain vulnerable at open-air speaking engagements and public events, which have been targeted by malicious actors seeking to advance political or ideological agendas and/or draw attention to unique personal grievances through violence

Canva #1 Scarsdale Westchester County, New York Over 90% of adults hold a bachelor’s degree or higher 15 Reasons Why New Yorkers Secretly Hate Living in New York State Canva Jobs don’t match the cost of living In upstate regions especially, salaries lag far behind the price tags on homes and groceries. You soon learn to take stable income where you can find it. Canva The taxes will drain your soul (and bank account) New York’s taxes aren’t just high—they’re legendary. Between property levies in Westchester and Nassau, state income tax pushing past 10%, and sales tax on nearly everything, your wallet takes a daily hit. Canva Winters are brutal When snow flies in October and April hits with another blizzard, you’ll wonder if spring ever arrives. Endless shovel duty, frozen windshields, and salt-crusted boots define the season upstate. Canva The NYC vs. Upstate divide It’s not just geography—it’s a whole different world. Funding, attention, and resources flood the city while upstate feels largely ignored Canva Albany feels like it’s from another planet What lawmakers do up there often feels disconnected from life down here—until you’re hit with a new law. Residents shrug, wondering if Albany even remembers what real New York looks like. Canva Everything is expensive Prices on groceries, gas, rent—even drive-through burgers—are noticeably sky-high. In New York, your dollar doesn’t get very far. Canva Crime is a growing concern Once-quiet suburbs are seeing thefts, drugs, and violence spike. Cities like Rochester, Syracuse, and Buffalo now regularly make national headlines. Canva The roads are a disaster Deep potholes, perpetual construction, and winter rot make driving a rough ride. It often feels like you need a survival guide, not a GPS. Canva The politics are polarizing Liberal NYC clashes hard with conservative rural and upstate values. That tension means lots of “You don’t get us” grumbling from both ends of the spectrum. Canva Leaving the state is a hassle Want to escape to warmer weather? Expect tolls, traffic, and long stretches of highway before you hit the sunshine. A quick getaway often turns into a full-blown expedition. Canva The migration is real Friends are packing up for Florida, the Carolinas, even Texas—where taxes are lower and the sun shines more. Every farewell makes New York feel a little smaller. Canva It’s hard to buy a home With low inventory, insane bidding wars, and sky-high taxes, homeownership feels out of reach for many locals. The dream inches farther away unless you’re ready to commute hours. Canva Small‑town gossip is next-level Privacy is basically a myth in the suburbs and villages. Show up to the store in your sweatpants and you’ll know it—everyone’s already texting about you. Canva There’s a love‑hate loyalty You’ll hear complaints from New Yorkers until the cows come home, but try moving them elsewhere and watch the pride return. Somehow, even when it’s driving you nuts, Empire State love never leaves. Canva The weather is all over the place One day you’re in tee-shirts, the next you’re digging out your car from snow. Planning anything here is always a roll of the dice.
